source.text: ወ*ይቤለኒ፡ ሄኖክ፡ ምንተ፡ ትስእል፡ በእንተ፡ መዓዛሁ፡ ለዝ፡ ዕፅ፡ ወትጠየቅ፡ ከመ፡ ታእምር።

translation.text: And he said to me[a], “Enoch, why do you ask about the fragrance of this tree, and inquire so that you may know?”

footnotes.text: Or 'concerning its scent.' The Ge'ez term refers to smell or fragrance; 'fragrance' was chosen for the elevated tone of the scene.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ *አውሣእክዎ፡ አነ፡ ሄኖክ፡ *እንዘ፡ እብል፡ በእንተ፡ ኵሉ፡ እፈቅድ፡ ኣእምር፡ ወፈድፋደ*ሰ፡ በእንተ*ዝ፡ ዕፅ።

translation.text: At that time I[a], Enoch, answered him, saying, “I desire to know about everything[b], but especially about this tree.”

footnotes.text: The Ge'ez wording at the end is somewhat difficult; the sense is that Enoch asks for fuller knowledge concerning the tree.
Or 'And at that time I, Enoch, answered and said, concerning all this, “I desire to know about this tree all the more.”'.

source.text: ወአውሥአ፡ እንዘ፡ ይብል፡ ዝንቱ፡ ደብር፡ ዘርኢከ፡ ነዋኅ፡ ዘርእሱ፡ ይመስል፡ መንበረ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ መንበሩ፡ ውእቱ፡ ኀበ፡ ይነብር፡ *ቅዱስ፡ ወዐቢይ፡ እግዚአ፡ ስብሐት፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዘለዓለም፡ ሶበ፡ ይወርድ፡ የኀውጻ፡ ለምድር፡ በሠናይ።

translation.text: And he answered me[a], saying, “This high mountain that you have seen, whose summit is like the throne of the Lord, is his throne, where the Holy and Great One, the Lord of Glory, the Eternal King[c][b], will dwell when he comes down to visit the earth with goodness.”

footnotes.text: Or 'whose top is like the throne of the Lord.' The Ge'ez wording may describe either the mountain's summit specifically or the mountain more generally in relation to the throne imagery.
The final phrase can also be understood as 'to inspect the earth for good' or 'to visit the earth in goodness.' The sense is a beneficent divine visitation, not merely movement from heaven to earth.
Or 'is the place where the Holy and Great Lord of Glory, the Eternal King, will sit'.

source.text: ወዝንቱሂ፡ ዕፀ፡ መዓዛ፡ ወአልሐዱ፡ ዘሥጋ፡ አልቦ፡ ሥልጣነ፡ ከመ፡ ይግሥሦ፡ እስከ፡ አመ፡ ዐቢይ፡ ኵነኔ፡ አመ፡ ይትቤቀል፡ ኵሎ፡ ወ*ይፌጽም፡ እስከ፡ ለዓለም፤ ዝኩ፡ ለጻድቃን፡ ወለትሑታን፡ ይትወሀብ።

translation.text: And this fragrant tree—no flesh has authority to touch it until the great judgment[a], when all will be avenged and brought to completion forever[d][c][b]; then it will be given to the righteous and the humble.

footnotes.text: Literally, 'no flesh has authority.' The phrase refers to mortal humans, not to flesh as a substance.
The clause after 'the great judgment' is difficult. The sense is that vengeance is carried out universally and the matter is brought to its full completion.

source.text: [እም]ፍሬ፡ ዚአሁ፡ [ይትወሀብ፡] ለኅሩያን፡ †ሐይወት፡† †*ወመንገለ፡ መስዕ፡† ይተከል፡ ዲበ፡ መካነ፡ ቅዱስ፡ መንገለ፡ ቤቱ፡ ለእግዚአ፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዘለዓለም።

translation.text: From its fruit life shall be given to the chosen ones[a], and it shall be planted toward the north[b], upon...

footnotes.text: The final phrase is textually difficult in this isolated witness. 'Toward the north, above' follows the surviving Ge'ez words literally; the implied reference may be to the tree's future planting location.

source.text: ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ ይትፌሥሑ፡ በፍሥሓ፡ ወይትሐሰዩ፡ ውስተ፡ ቅዱስ፡ ወይበውኡ፡ *መዓዛ፡ ሎቱ፡ በ፯አዕጽምቲሆሙ፡ ወሕይወተ፡ ብዙኀ፡ የሐይዉ፡ በዲበ፡ ምድር፡ በከመ፡ ሐይዉ፡ አበዊከ፡ ወበመዋዕሊሆሙ፡ ኀዘን፡ ወ*ጻማም፡ ወፃዕር፡ ወመቅሠፍት፡ ኢይገሥሦሙ።
ውእተ፡ ጊዜ፡ ባረክዎ፡ ለአምላከ፡ ስብሐት፡ ንጉሥ፡ ዘለዓለም፡ እስመ፡ አስተዳለወ፡ *ለሰብእ፡ ከመዝ፡ ጻድቃን፡ ወከመዝ፡ ፈጠረ፡ ወይቤ፡ የሀብዎሙ።
